title: The ideal gas equation PV = nRT
summary: One equation joins P, V, T and the amount of gas: change any slider and watch the others follow.
alt: A cylinder of gas with sliders for the number of molecules, temperature and volume, and live readings of pressure and P×V divided by N×T.

gas.label: Gas molecules
gas.text: The molecules of the gas (colour = speed: blue slow, red fast).

th.label: PV ÷ (N T)
th.text: This ratio is the same for every state of an ideal gas.

me.label: Live reading
me.text: What the simulated gas shows right now.

steps.title: Three laws, one equation
steps.text: Boyle: \( P \propto 1/V \). Charles: \( V \propto T \). Gay-Lussac: \( P \propto T \). And the more gas, the more pressure: \( P \propto N \). Put them all together: \( \dfrac{PV}{NT} = \text{constant} \).

steps.title: Change the volume
steps.text: Halve the volume. P doubles and V halves, so P × V is unchanged. The ratio PV ÷ NT stays at **{{(Pm*L/8)/(n*T/12000)|2}}**.

steps.title: Change the temperature
steps.text: Now heat the gas at constant volume. P goes up in proportion to T; the ratio is still **{{(Pm*L/8)/(n*T/12000)|2}}**.

steps.title: Change the amount of gas
steps.text: Double the number of molecules: P doubles. The constant stays the same because we divide by N too. Written per mole it becomes \( PV = nRT \).

steps.title: Per mole or per molecule
steps.text: With **n moles**: \( PV = nRT \) where \( R = 8.31\ \text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1} \). With **N molecules**: \( PV = NkT \) where the **Boltzmann constant** is \( k = R/N_A \). Play with all three sliders.

formulas.title: Ideal gas equation
formulas.text: P in pascal, V in m³, n in moles, T in kelvin, R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.

formulas.title: Boltzmann constant
formulas.text: PV = NkT when you count molecules N instead of moles n.

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: How many moles of an ideal gas are in a **2 m³** container at **300 K** and **1.5 × 10⁵ Pa**? (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹) Give your answer to the nearest mole.

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: The gas shows **1 P₀** at **V₀** and **300 K**. Both V and T are doubled. What is the pressure in P₀?
challenges.explain: T doubles (×2) and V doubles (÷2), so P is unchanged: **1 P₀**.

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: In \( PV = NkT \), what does the Boltzmann constant k equal?
challenges.hint: k is the gas constant for one molecule.

takeaways: It combines Boyle, Charles and Gay-Lussac (and the effect of the amount of gas).
Always use **kelvin** and SI units (pascal, m³).

notes.title: Connects to
notes.text: The three laws are special cases: **fix T** → Boyle (isothermal), **fix P** → Charles (isobaric), **fix V** → Gay-Lussac (isochoric). Next, see how a changing volume does **work** (W = PΔV) and how that links to the **first law**.
